description: Shared correctness fixtures (docs/benchmark-correctness-fixtures.md). One xorshift64 stream (seed=42, n=1000000) generates records with two 'hot' fields (hotA, hotB) and a dataset-specific number of 'cold' fields, in strict per-record order: hotA, hotB, cold[0..coldWords). Four layouts (AoS heap objects, AoS packed/off-heap, SoA primitive vectors, hybrid hot/cold split) store the SAME generated values differently. Both languages must reproduce every value below exactly, AND every layout of a given dataset must produce the IDENTICAL hotSum and coldChecksum — layout changes storage, never the data. Change a value here only together with both test files.

semantics.xorshift64: x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >>> 7 (unsigned/logical); x ^= x << 17 (64-bit wrapping, unsigned interpretation throughout)
semantics.generationOrder: for each record index i in [0,n): x=xorshift64(x); hotA[i]=x unsigned-mod 1000000; x=xorshift64(x); hotB[i]=x unsigned-mod 1000000; then for w in [0,coldWords): x=xorshift64(x); cold[i][w]=x unsigned-mod 1000000
semantics.hotSum: wrapping 64-bit sum of (hotA[i]+hotB[i]) over all i — the layout-invariance oracle: every layout of a dataset must produce this exact value
semantics.coldChecksum: checksum*31 + v (64-bit wrapping) over every cold[i][w] in row-major (i then w) order — proves cold data survived the layout unchanged
semantics.checksumHotA: checksum*31 + v (64-bit wrapping) over hotA alone
semantics.checksumHotB: checksum*31 + v (64-bit wrapping) over hotB alone

operationDefinition: one benchmark operation = one full pass over the declared dataset's 1,000,000 records, accumulating the wrapping sum of (hotA[i] + hotB[i]) via the layout's own hot-field access pattern; cold fields are never touched by the timed operation (this is what 'read-mostly scan over selected fields' means) — the returned sum is consumed to block dead-code elimination

recordShape.coldFieldType: i64 (u64-domain values 0..999999, same domain as hot for a uniform generator)
